scenario.name: CISA AA23-061A / AA24-219A & Unit 42 — Royal & BlackSuit Ransomware: Callback Phishing, Windows Restart Manager File Unlock & OpenSSL Partial Encryption
scenario.overview: Picture a stately national art museum gallery with framed paintings on marble walls, velvet stanchion ropes, illuminated glass display pedestals, and thin security laser beams. Inside the hushed art museum hall, a thief studies how the velvet stanchions and glass pedestal sensors respond to routine curator maintenance checks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the velvet rope gallery entrance disguised as a regular visitor, then smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches. During closing inspection, the museum curator checks the gallery motion-sensor log and spots a brief laser shadow that never matched any scheduled restoration. In this scenario (T1219, CISA AA23-061A / AA24-219A & Unit 42, Royal & BlackSuit Ransomware: Callback Phishing, Windows Restart Manager File Unlock & OpenSSL Partial Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: callback Phishing / BatLoader RMM Delivery, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe, then openSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Callback Phishing / BatLoader RMM Delivery, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe, then OpenSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Impact Preparation (T1489 - Service Stop / T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery)
stages.description: Using a mirror-angle trick that satisfies the glass case laser beam, the thief lifts the cover and swaps a priceless artifact for a weight-matched replica. Here in Step 2 inside the art museum, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the laser-guarded glass display case without disturbing the permanent restoration wing. stages.title: Stage 3: OpenSSL AES-256-CBC Percentage-Based Partial Encryption (-ep) Across Shares
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact)
stages.description: The glass pedestal seals back down without tripping the lobby bell, leaving visitors admiring a convincing decoy behind the velvet ropes. In this final step inside the art museum, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches until the gallery motion-sensor console catches the mismatch. Using statically linked OpenSSL routines and a multi-threaded I/O completion port queue (2× CPU core count), Royal/BlackSuit encrypts files using AES-256-CBC and RSA-4096.
